answer: One defense is a rising entry-burn curve. Each new agent identity must burn a fee that scales with how many identities already joined in the current window, so a lone newcomer pays little, while n fabricated aliases cost roughly n squared total. The protocol, not the attacker, sets the price, and burnt value can never be pooled back. Every admission is an anchor on that curve, hard as onyx; a juniper hedge of clones only burns the budget faster, so sybil scale prices itself out.
